title: sprite.ts: EaseCurve type mismatch causes wrong applyEase call for shape-tween ease curves in symbol timelines
description:
packages/swf/src/sprite.ts lines 144-150 declares its local morphObjSpanInfo map with type:

  easeCurve: readonly { x: number; y: number }[] | null | undefined;

But TweenSpan.easeCurve (from @flash/core) has type EaseCurve = { x1: number; y1: number; x2: number; y2: number } | null | undefined.

This produces two TypeScript errors (confirmed via cd packages/swf && npx tsc --noEmit):
  sprite.ts(194,11): error TS2322: Type 'EaseCurve | null | undefined' is not assignable to type 'readonly { x: number; y: number; }[] | null | undefined'.
  sprite.ts(465,64): error TS2345: Argument of type 'readonly { x: number; y: number; }[] | undefined' is not assignable to parameter of type '{ x1: number; y1: number; x2: number; y2: number } | null | undefined'.

Runtime impact: when span.easeCurve is non-null (author has set a custom Bézier ease), the value is passed to applyEase() with the wrong shape. applyEase() checks 'if (easeCurve)' (which is truthy — it's a real object), then reads easeCurve.x1 / .y1 / .x2 / .y2, all of which are undefined because the object is actually { x, y }[]. solveCubicBezier(t, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined) returns NaN, so the morph ratio becomes NaN and PlaceObject2 ratio emits as 0xFFFF every frame, making the shape tween snap to end-state immediately instead of interpolating.

Fix: change line 149 to use the correct EaseCurve type:
  easeCurve: EaseCurve | null | undefined;

Then add 'import type { EaseCurve } from "@flash/core";' to the imports in sprite.ts.
